jobs.title: Air Pollution Specialist
jobs.description:
Job Description And Duties

The Regulatory and Risk Modeling (RRM) Section within the Modeling and Meteorology Branch (MMB) is responsible for conducting the triennial California Air Toxics Assessment (CATA) and maintaining the CATA visualization mapping tool and data portal, as well as providing microscale to statewide air quality and toxics modeling support for the Air Board's various regulatory programs, including the community air protection program, airborne toxic control measures, state implementation plans for lead, NO2, and SO2, the air toxics hot spots program, and emergency response support.

The APS, working as part of a team, will support CATA through preparing and QA/QC'ing model inputs, such as emissions inventory, meteorology, and boundary conditions, conduct air dispersion and chemical transport modeling, investigate emerging air toxics (e.g., PCBTF, EtO, acrolein), translate ambient exposure to estimated cancer risk, analyze model outputs, and summarize findings for both technical and public audiences. In addition, the APS will work closely with lead staff on supporting the day-to-day operation of the High Performance Computing (HPC) Linux modeling cluster CATA modeling relies on. This could include monitoring storage and compute node usage, troubleshooting any issues that may arise, and onboarding new users.

You will find additional information about the job in the Duty Statement
.

Working Conditions

This position may be eligible for hybrid in-office work and in-state telework. The amount of telework is at the agency's discretion and is based on the California Air Resources Boards' (CARB) current telework policy. While the CARB may support telework, some in-person attendance is also required.?

The positions at the CARB may be eligible for telework with in-person attendance based on the operational needs of the position?under Government Code 14200 for eligible applicants residing in California, subject to the candidate meeting telework eligibility criteria outlined in the CalEPA telework policy and/or future program need. Employees not residing in California are not eligible for telework. Regardless of hybrid telework eligibility, all employees may be required to report to the position’s designated headquarters location at their own expense, as indicated on their duty statement.

Effective July 1, 2025, the California Department of Human Resources (CalHR) implemented the Personal Leave Program 2025 (PLP 2025). PLP 2025 directs that each employee shall receive a 3 percent reduction in pay in exchange for 5 hours PLP 2025 leave credits, monthly. The salary range(s) included in the job advertisement do not reflect the 3 percent reduction in pay.

Position located in a high-rise building
Requires being in a stationary position, consistent with office work, for extended periods.
Standard office environment (for example, artificial lighting, controlled temperature, etc.)
Daily use of a personal computer, office equipment, and/or telephone.
Travel may be required.

jobs.title: Early-Career Hazardous Materials Consultant - Perth, WA
jobs.description:
Build on your asbestos surveying experience and grow your specialist career
Work alongside industry experts who will support your technical development
Perth based with opportunities to work on diverse projects across WA and beyond

An exciting opportunity for an early-career Hazardous Materials Consultant to develop their skills and experience within our established Workplace Health and Safety team. You'll gain exposure to a diverse range of projects, supported by experienced professionals who are committed to helping you grow.

Why Join Our Team?

Joining our team means you'll work alongside experienced scientists, engineers and specialist consultants, gaining valuable exposure to hazardous materials and occupational hygiene projects across a range of industries.

We provide specialist services to Tier 1 Mining and Oil & Gas companies, Defence, Federal and State government agencies, and other major clients. Our projects range from local site investigations to some of the largest and most recognised projects across WA and the NT, with opportunities for exposure to international work.

Working closely with the broader Tetra Tech family of companies, we combine technical expertise with practical, sustainable solutions to help our clients manage complex environmental and workplace health challenges.

You'll be joining a supportive team where you can build on your existing fieldwork experience, broaden your technical knowledge and develop your career with guidance from highly qualified professionals.

About The Role

With a strong pipeline of projects across our national Workplace Health and Safety team, we're looking for an early-career Hazardous Materials Consultant to join our growing Perth team.

This opportunity is ideally suited to someone with at least 2 years' experience in asbestos surveying and hazardous materials inspections who is looking to take the next step in their consulting career.

You'll be involved in a mix of fieldwork, technical reporting and client engagement, with opportunities to develop your skills across hazardous materials assessments and occupational hygiene services.

Your Responsibilities Will Include

Undertaking asbestos and hazardous materials surveys, assessments and site inspections
Conducting field investigations, sampling and monitoring activities
Assisting with occupational hygiene monitoring and asbestos fibre counting
Supporting asbestos removal and remediation projects, including site inspections and clearance activities where appropriately qualified
Collecting, recording and interpreting field data, ensuring accuracy and quality
Preparing hazardous materials registers, survey reports and other technical documentation
Liaising with clients, contractors and colleagues to support safe and effective project delivery
Assisting senior consultants with project coordination and delivery

About You

We're looking for someone who enjoys hands-on fieldwork, has a genuine interest in hazardous materials and is keen to continue learning and developing their technical expertise.

Ideally, You'll Bring

A minimum of 2 years' practical experience in asbestos surveying, hazardous materials inspections or a closely related field
Qualifications in a relevant science discipline, occupational hygiene or a related field
A sound understanding of asbestos identification, sampling and hazardous materials assessment practices
Experience preparing asbestos registers, survey reports or other technical documentation
Good communication skills and the confidence to engage with clients and contractors on site
Strong attention to detail, a practical approach to problem-solving and a commitment to safe work practices
A willingness to learn, contribute to the team and develop your technical capabilities
The flexibility to travel to regional and remote sites as required
A current full Australian driver's licence
Australian citizenship or permanent residency to meet Defence project requirements

Experience in occupational hygiene monitoring, asbestos air monitoring or fibre counting would be advantageous, but is not essential.

Holding a Licensed Asbestos Assessor qualification, or working towards eligibility, would also be highly regarded.

Please note:
This role will involve fieldwork and travel to regional and remote locations, including occasional periods away from home.

The Perks You’ll Love

Work-Life Balance: While this role is essentially field based, you have the ability to buy extra leave giving you up to 8 weeks leave per year!
Diverse Projects: Work across a wide variety of projects, clients, and sectors
Growth Opportunities: Professional development, coaching, and mentorship from our top experts
Memberships: Professional memberships to help you stay ahead in your field
Recognition: Our reward and recognition program makes sure your hard work doesn’t go unnoticed
Ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan
Parental Leave: Paid leave for both primary and secondary caregivers
Support: Employee assistance program for you and your immediate family
Travel Discounts: Great deals through our corporate traveller program
Car Leasing: Take advantage of novated vehicle leasing options

About Us

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation. 

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global  1 Billion People Challenge , which tracks how our 100,000+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.

jobs.title: Early-Career Environmental Scientist - Contaminated Land
jobs.description:
Great opportunity to join our long-established Contaminated Land consulting group in Perth
Enjoy mentoring and access to our senior specialists
Diverse projects and learning opportunities across multiple sectors and clients

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.

About The Role

As an early-career professional, you’ll work alongside our team of experienced environmental professionals who are dedicated to helping you grow and succeed. You'll gain hands-on experience in assessing and remediating contaminated land, and developing essential skills in client engagement, proposal development, and project management.

You’ll work on a diverse range of exciting and challenging contaminated land projects across multiple industries including Defence, Mining, Oil & Gas and Government.

This is a great opportunity to grow a rewarding career in a global consultancy that values innovation, collaboration, and excellence in environmental solutions.

Key Responsibilities

Conduct fieldwork for a variety of contaminated site investigation and remediation projects, including soil, groundwater, surface water, and ground gas sampling.
Observe, guide, and document site remediation activities to ensure compliance and effectiveness.
Manage, interpret, and ensure the quality of data through rigorous quality assurance and quality control processes.
Assist in writing proposals, project correspondence, and technical reports to communicate findings and recommendations effectively.

About You

To thrive in the role, you should ideally demonstrate the following:

A degree in Environmental Engineering, Environmental Science, or Geosciences.
A minimum of 12 months gained in contaminated land fieldwork.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, enabling you to convey complex information clearly and effectively.
Excellent interpersonal skills with a collaborative team-oriented mindset.
Genuine enthusiasm for producing high-quality work that delivers practical solutions for our clients.
A commitment to maintaining high health and safety standards for yourself, your team, and any contractors involved.
Willingness to undertake remote fieldwork across Australia.
Permanent residency in Australia.
An unrestricted Australian driver’s license.

If you’re keen to build your specialist consulting career and contribute to meaningful environmental projects, we’d love you to apply!

You’ll Enjoy These Benefits

Work-Life balance: We help you create space for other important aspects of your life with study breaks and leave purchase plans allowing you to enjoy up to 8 weeks of annual leave per year!
Diverse project opportunities: Work on a wide range of projects across various clients and sectors, keeping your experience fresh and engaging.
Professional growth: Access ongoing development opportunities, including coaching from our approachable technical experts and support for professional memberships.
Employee ownership: Participate in our employee stock purchase plan and share in the company’s success.
Paid parental leave: Enjoy paid parental leave for both primary and secondary caregivers.
Wellbeing support: Access our Employee Assistance Program (EAP), available to all staff and their immediate families.

About Us

Tetra Tech Coffey provides high-end environmental, geotechnical, digital, and engineering design consulting services in Australia, New Zealand and Papua New Guinea. Every day, our people come together to solve complex challenges for our clients.

With over 30,000 Tetra Tech colleagues across 550 offices globally, we deliver projects that improve lives through science, technology, and innovation.

Our commitment to creating lasting, measurable value is reflected in our global1 Billion People Challenge, which tracks how our 100,000+ annual projects benefit people and communities around the world.
